mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, prompting central bank intervention and reducing corporate earnings expectations, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 5% YoY and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 2.0%, it indicates a policy misstep that fuels stagflation fears, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the CPIAUCSL YoY > 5% and FEDFUNDS < 2.0% condition.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with HOUST decline during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where RSAFS rises by at least 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 indicates robust manufacturing activity, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where INDPRO exceeds 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed 200,000, it indicates labor market overheating, prompting aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS above 200.0.

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) has an inverse relationship with S&P 500 returns: lower rates reduce discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with FEDFUNDS below 1.0%.
